claim_audit.claim: E1a: M_kink = 0.9428090346 and omega_s = 1.2247448677, CALIBRATED
claim_audit.note: Collocation BVP gives M = 0.9428090416 (rel. err. 3e-15), Chebyshev omega_s = 1.2247448717.
Fourier + RK4 code with x0 = 15 and its own box gives 0.260066 (dt = 0.02 bracket 0.26006-0.260066). The 2.6e-4 offset from the [summary] target is common to both codes, so it is not numerical.

claim_audit.claim: E1b: first two-bounce window [0.19256, 0.20343], >= 3 windows narrowing toward v_c
E1b: Manton et al. 2021 quote the first window as 0.1920-0.2029
claim_audit.note: Read in arXiv:2106.05153v2 here: "the first 2-bounce window occurs for 0.1920 < vin < 0.2029".

claim_audit.claim: E1c: (omega, v) = (0.99, 0.43) produces a pair, CALIBRATED; "the pair is real: it is still separating at 1.5T"
claim_audit.note: The call is not reproducible. The original code itself (unmodified copy) produces at only 4 of 10 (dx, dt) settings: yes at (0.1, 0.04) [t = 1160], (0.1, 0.02) [780], (0.025, 0.005) and (0.0125, 0.005) [840]; no at (0.1, 0.01), (0.05, 0.02), (0.05, 0.01), (0.05, 0.005), (0.025, 0.01) and (0.025, 0.0025). The two independent, higher-order-in-time codes give no pair up to 1.5T (FD6+RK4 dx 0.08; spectral dx0.1_dt0.02: no pair, dx0.05_dt0.02: no pair, dx0.1_dt0.01: no pair). The point was never resolution-checked in E1, and its formation time (1160) is the latest of all 80 producers (median 120). It is a sensitive point, not a calibration point. The DSV-like event does exist 0.02 lower: (0.99, 0.41) forms a pair at t = 590 in the spectral code at (dx, dt) = (0.1, 0.02), (0.05, 0.02) and (0.1, 0.01), and in the finest original setting (0.025, 0.005).

claim_audit.claim: E1c reproduces DSV Fig. 2 band by band, including the example point
claim_audit.note: Band location and trend are reproduced for omega = 0.90-0.98 by both codes: 91% call agreement on 160 common points, FD6 Spearman -0.94. At v step 0.02 the original hits 14 of DSV's 22 producing points with 7 false positives (FD6: 16 and 5). The omega = 0.99 column is not converged: original code, v 0.38-0.48, gives producers {0.39, 0.41, 0.43} at (0.1, 0.04), {0.43} at (0.1, 0.02) and none at (0.05, 0.02). The spectral code gives a converged producer at v = 0.41 (dx 0.05: pair since t=590.0); FD6 gives v = 0.40 on its step-0.02 grid. So DSV's omega = 0.99 production near v ~ 0.4 is reproduced, but at 0.41, not at the quoted 0.43.

claim_audit.claim: E1c: dx = 0.05 rerun agrees on 74 of 78 calls; the four disagreements are band-edge points
claim_audit.note: True as counted, but the omega = 0.99 column agrees only trivially: its producers at dx = 0.1 (0.41, 0.43) are not on the dx = 0.05 grid, and the dx = 0.05 column has no producer at all. The example point was never resolution-checked.

claim_audit.claim: E1c: trend to lower v as omega rises, pass-through at high v, none above omega = 0.99
claim_audit.note: FD6: Spearman -0.94; 0/18 producing at v >= 0.86; 0/6 at omega = 0.995.
Not on the FD6 grid. The original dx = 0.05 rerun keeps v = 0.82 empty between producing 0.80 and 0.84.

claim_audit.claim: E1d: no production below 2 M_kink (0 of 19,526 runs), CALIBRATED
claim_audit.note: 0 of 1485 (FD6) and 0 in the spectral runs. This is a sanity check, not a literature calibration, so the CALIBRATED label is a misuse (minor).

claim_audit.claim: E1d: producing fraction vs E/2M table; no coarse producer with A <= 0.3
claim_audit.note: FD6 on the same 1485 points: 587 vs 564 producing, every band within 0.07, 0 producers with A <= 0.3. Point agreement 83% (80% at E > 2M) equals the original's own dx-halving agreement (80%). 90 random coarse points (A >= 0.3), spectral vs original 73% agreement (E > 2M: 72%), spectral vs FD6 84%, FD6 vs original 80%.

claim_audit.claim: E1d: lowest resolution-checked producers E/2M = 1.86 (baseline phi_t, (0.8, 2, 0.5)) and 2.70 (one-way phi_t, (0.6, 4, 0.5))
claim_audit.note: FD6 lowest producer is the same point at 1.858. Spectral: (0.8, 2, 0.5) produces at dx 0.1 (E/2M = 1.8584) and dx 0.05 (True); own one-way construction (0.6, 4, 0.5): E/2M = 2.7030, produces True / True at dx 0.1 / 0.05. The raw 1.79 point is not a robust producer in any code.

claim_audit.claim: E1d: single packets with A >~ 0.4 fold on their own (65% of producing coarse points)
claim_audit.note: FD6 sample: 57/80 self-fold, 87% agreement with the original. Spectral sigma = 16 scan: k=0.25: first self-folding A = 0.425, k=1: first self-folding A = 0.425. A simple mechanism the report leaves unanalysed: the field at a trough, phi = -1 - A, already has potential energy above the barrier V(0) = 1/4 when A > sqrt2 - 1 = 0.414.

claim_audit.claim: E1d: the production boundary is ragged (fractured), CONFIRMED
claim_audit.note: Qualitatively reproduced: on the sigma = 16, k = 1 line FD6 and the original both switch 17 times with onset A = 0.375 (80% point agreement). On the k = 2 line both are non-monotonic with the same onset and the same gap at A = 0.45-0.5, but with 9 vs 17 switches. Region, hole and switch counts are not converged numbers.

claim_audit.claim: E1d: slower packets produce more at matched energy (rho -0.82 to -0.88), CONFIRMED; seed claim "low speed holds"
claim_audit.note: The correlation reproduces (FD6: -0.82, -0.93, -0.92), but it is an amplitude effect. At matched energy slow packets have larger A (mean A 0.80-0.90 at v_g <= 0.47 against 0.36-0.42 at v_g >= 0.82 in the [2, 4) band). At fixed A (E > 2M) no amplitude level shows a significant negative speed trend in the original data (one marginal case, A = 0.5, p = 0.045) and none for collision-needed production. In the independent FD6 data the only significant fixed-A trend runs the other way (A = 1.2, rho = +0.75, p = 0.02). Computed by xc2_confound.py.

claim_audit.claim: E1d: no width preference at matched energy (NOT SUPPORTED)
E1e: N_min lambda/m^2 = 1.24 (N = E/m), 1.69 (N_lin) Gaussian; 4.78 / 3.93 DSV; floor 2/3
claim_audit.note: Scaling N lambda/m^2 = E~/(2 sqrt2) re-derived. The values are reproduced from independently built initial data (1.2389 / 1.6879; 4.7805 / 3.9278). They are upper bounds within the scanned families, as the report says.

claim_audit.claim: Seed section 2 AMENDED: "2M is a floor, not where classical production starts; a classical field needs extra energy for radiation and kink motion"
claim_audit.note: True only within the scanned families. The phi^4 equation is time-reversal invariant: reversing a slow (v << v_c) kink-antikink capture, whose bion radiates its energy away, gives radiation-only initial data that make a pair with E = 2M gamma(v) -> 2M. So the classical infimum is 2M. 1.86 / 2.70 / 7.2 x 2M are family-specific upper bounds on the onset. The seed's floor statement is consistent with E1 (no violation), so CONFIRMED, plus a note on generic data, fits better than AMENDED.

claim_audit.claim: Seed section 4: a small, spread-out packet is linear and passes through, CONFIRMED
claim_audit.note: No producer with A <= 0.3 in either code.

claim_audit.claim: Seed section 4: pile in enough energy and the packet can fold, AMENDED (amplitude, not energy, controls it)
claim_audit.note: Consistent with the local over-barrier threshold A* = 0.41 and with both codes' fraction-vs-energy curves.

claim_audit.claim: Seed section 4: DSV trains make pairs over a wide range, "most easily at low speed", CONFIRMED
claim_audit.note: DSV and E1c both show production in an omega-dependent velocity band with nothing below it (omega = 0.90: no producer for v < 0.73 in the original grid). The lowest-energy producers are at omega = 0.90-0.95 and v = 0.62-0.73 (E/2M ~ 7), not at low v. What holds is that the band moves to lower v as the pulses weaken. AMENDED is the earned verdict.

claim_audit.claim: Seed sections 4 / 7.1: ragged boundary, CONFIRMED
claim_audit.note: See the E1d ragged row.

claim_audit.claim: Seed section 8: classical pair needs N ~ (1.2-2) m^2/lambda quanta, QUANTIFIED; exponential suppression OPEN
claim_audit.note: Numbers reproduced; OPEN is appropriate.

issues.description: E1c headline "DSV example (0.99, 0.43) produces a pair (appears at t ~ 1160), still separating at 1.5T: CALIBRATED" is not demonstrated. The point is resolution-sensitive and was never resolution-checked. The original code itself produces at 4 of 10 (dx, dt) settings, with no monotone trend down to dt = 0.0025: (0.1, 0.04) yes; (0.1, 0.02) yes; (0.1, 0.01) no; (0.05, 0.02 / 0.01 / 0.005) no; (0.025, 0.01) no; (0.025, 0.005) yes; (0.025, 0.0025) no; (0.0125, 0.005) yes. Two independent, higher-order-in-time codes give no pair at all. The report's "the pair is real: it is still separating at 1.5T" generalises from one discretisation. The dx = 0.05 rerun's 74/78 agreement is trivial in the omega = 0.99 column, whose producing v (0.41, 0.43) are not on that grid; at dx = 0.05 the original finds no omega = 0.99 producer at v = 0.38-0.48.
issues.suggested_fix: Re-label the row: (0.99, 0.43) is a sensitive point whose call depends on dx and dt in every code (3 of 3 independent runs give no pair). Report that a converged DSV-like producer exists at (0.99, 0.41): pair at t = 590 in the spectral code at three (dx, dt) settings and in the finest original setting. Replace "the pair is real" with that statement, and add a resolution check for every map point that carries a verdict.

issues.description: Seed section 4 DSV claim marked CONFIRMED although its "most easily at low speed" part contradicts E1c's own map. At fixed omega there is no production below the band (omega = 0.90: none for v < 0.73), and the lowest-energy producers sit at v = 0.62-0.73.
issues.suggested_fix: AMENDED: production occurs in an omega-dependent velocity band that moves to lower v as the pulses weaken; it is not easiest at low speed.

issues.description: The E1d "slower produces more at matched energy" result (CONFIRMED, and "low speed holds" in the seed-claim evidence) is confounded with amplitude. At matched energy slow packets carry larger A, and production is controlled by A (self-folding needs A >~ 0.4). At fixed A no level shows a significant negative speed trend (original: one marginal case, A = 0.5, p = 0.045; FD6: only A = 1.2, rho = +0.75), and collision-needed production shows none at any A. In the one-way form the collision-needed speed test is NOT SUPPORTED (results.json), yet the seed-claim text says low speed holds in both forms.
issues.suggested_fix: State that the matched-energy speed correlation is explained by amplitude. Report the fixed-A test, under which no speed preference is found. Mark the PLAN speed prediction NOT SUPPORTED as a speed effect.

issues.description: Seed section 2 verdict AMENDED rests on "in classical dynamics 2M is a floor and not the onset; a classical field needs extra energy for radiation and kink motion". That is true only of the scanned families. Time reversal of a slow sub-v_c capture gives radiation-only data that make a pair at E -> 2M, so the classical infimum is 2M itself.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep the data (no producer below 2M; family onsets 1.86 / 2.70 / 7.2 x 2M as upper bounds) and either mark the claim CONFIRMED (floor holds) with a note on generic initial data, or restrict the amendment explicitly to the scanned families.

issues.description: CALIBRATED is used for the energy-conservation sanity check (no production below 2M); PLAN defines CALIBRATED as reproducing a literature target.

Region, hole and switch counts of the slices appear in the headline and seed-claim evidence as numbers, but they are not converged. On the sigma = 16, k = 2 line the independent code switches 9 times against the original's 17 (same onset, same gap). The report says this in the text but still quotes the counts as results.
issues.suggested_fix: Quote the counts as illustrative only, and lead with the robust statements: onset A, non-monotonic lines in both codes, production fractions.

issues.description: The self-folding mechanism is called unanalysed, but the observed threshold (minimum A 0.375-0.425) matches a one-line estimate: a trough at phi = -1 - A has potential energy above the barrier 1/4 when A > sqrt2 - 1 = 0.414. Most E1d production (65%) is this local over-barrier effect rather than collision dynamics, which limits what the fraction-vs-energy curves say about collisions.
issues.suggested_fix: Add the estimate and separate collision-needed statistics in the headline.

issues.description: The E1c table simplifies DSV Fig. 2 in places. Omega = 0.95 is given as 0.64-0.77; the figure shows gaps (about 0.64-0.65, 0.67-0.70, 0.72-0.73, 0.75-0.77). Point-level overlap with DSV is only about 2/3.
issues.suggested_fix: Quote the hit / false-positive counts rather than "band by band".

issues.description: The report has no diagnosis for the 2.6e-4 v_c offset. The independent spectral code (other x0, box and integrator) lands within 1e-5 of the original, so the offset lies in the [summary] target, not in either computation.

summary: Independent recomputation with two different codes (6th-order FD + RK4; Fourier exact-linear 4th-order splitting) plus collocation and Chebyshev solvers. E1a, E1b (v_c 0.260066 vs 0.26006; first window to 1e-5), the E1c map trend, pass-through and omega > 0.99 null, all E1d statistics (564 vs 587 producing coarse runs; band fractions within 0.07; zero producers below 2M or with A <= 0.3; the same lowest producers; self-folding; ragged lines) and the E1e quanta counts are confirmed. Point-level E1d calls agree 73-84% between codes, the same as the original's own dx-halving agreement (80%). One headline calibration is not demonstrated: the DSV example point (0.99, 0.43) is resolution-sensitive. The original code produces it at 4 of 10 (dx, dt) settings, the independent codes never do; a converged DSV-like producer exists at (0.99, 0.41). Three seed-level verdicts are overstated: section 4 DSV "most easily at low speed"; the E1d low-speed preference, which is an amplitude confound; and the section 2 AMENDED rationale, which is family-specific since the classical infimum is 2M by time reversal.
